answer: Make each identity bet on the jury. Each epoch every seat publishes a sealed forecast of how many submissions juries fail, hashed as a cipher, opened after grading; weight accrues only from calibration, a Brier score over twenty rounds. Where N texts are cheap, N forecasts are not: one is right only if the model behind it read the room. A ring sharing one forecast has correlated error, and the scorer reads clusters, not seats: one bad guess drags the lagoon down. Newcomers climb slowly, uncalibrated, but a mirror reflecting nothing pays nothing and the attacker pays inference per seat.
